title: Comments in C++

visuals.title: Match each comment form to its use

pairs.meaning: Single-line comment: ends at the end of the line
Multi-line comment: can cover many lines
Commenting out code to switch it off for a while
Explains WHY the code does something
Repeats the obvious, such as 'add 1 to x'

goal: After this you can write single-line and multi-line comments, comment out code, and write comments that actually help the reader.
warmup: When you borrow a friend's notebook, small notes in the margin like 'important for exam' or 'check this formula' make it easy to follow. The teacher does not mark those notes as part of the answer. Comments in code are margin notes for humans. The computer ignores them completely.
definition: A comment is text inside the program that the compiler ignores. It is written for people who read the code (including you next month). C++ has two kinds: a single-line comment that starts with // and runs to the end of the line, and a multi-line comment that starts with /* and ends with */.
howItWorks: Press Play to see that comment lines are skipped and do nothing. Only real statements run. Use comments to say what a block does and why. Do not comment every obvious line. You can also put // in front of a statement to switch it off for a while without deleting it. This is called commenting out code.

variations.when: One line, or the end of a line of code
Many lines, or a small note in the middle of a line
Top of a program: purpose, author, date
Temporarily switch off a statement to test the rest

mistakes.error: expected primary-expression before '/' token (comments cannot be nested)
no compiler error, but a wrong or old comment is worse than no comment

examTips: The compiler completely ignores comments; they never change the output.
// ends at the end of the line. /* ... */ can span many lines.
Multi-line comments cannot be nested: the first */ ends the whole comment.
Good comments explain why, not just what. Do not comment every obvious line.
To find which line causes a problem, comment out code and run the rest.
romanSummary: Comment ek note hai jo compiler ignore karta hai, ye insaano ke parhne ke liye hota hai.
// single-line comment hai, ye line ke end tak chalta hai.
/* ... */ multi-line comment hai, ye kai lines tak ho sakta hai.
Code ko temporarily band karne ke liye us ke aage // laga do.
Acha comment batata hai ke kaam kyun kiya gaya, har aasan line par comment na likho.

practice.prompt: Which symbol starts a single-line comment?
practice.explanation: // starts a comment that runs to the end of the line.

practice.prompt:
Fill in the blank to end the multi-line comment:

/* This is a long comment ______
practice.hint: It is the reverse of how it starts.
practice.explanation: A multi-line comment starts with /* and ends with */.

practice.hint: Everything after // on a line is ignored.
practice.explanation: The cout for Y is inside a comment, so only X and Z are printed, next to each other: XZ.
The comment must end with */. Otherwise the compiler reports an unterminated comment.

practice.hint: Is the assignment x = 10 really executed?
practice.explanation: x = 10 is inside a comment, so it never runs. x stays 2.

practice.prompt:
Fill in the blank to switch off this line without deleting it:

______ cout << "Debug";
practice.explanation: Putting // in front turns the line into a comment, so it does not run.

practice.prompt: Write a program with a header comment (program name and author) that prints Welcome to UMT, and a short comment before the cout.
practice.hint: Use /* */ for the header and // for the short note.
practice.explanation: Comments do not change the output; they only explain the code.

practice.hint: Only the first assignment is real code.
practice.explanation: Only a = a + 1 runs, so a becomes 2. The other two lines are comments.

quiz.prompt: What does the compiler do with a comment?
Which is a valid multi-line comment?
quiz.hint: It starts with a slash and a star.

options: One that repeats every line in words
One that explains why the code does something
quiz.answer: One that explains why the code does something
quiz.explanation: Good comments explain the reason, not the obvious.

options: Does nothing, the line is commented out
quiz.answer: Does nothing, the line is commented out
quiz.hint: // turns the whole line into a comment.
quiz.explanation: Commented-out code is ignored by the compiler.

quiz.prompt: Why does /* a /* b */ c */ cause an error?
options: The word c is not allowed
It does not cause an error
quiz.explanation: The first */ closes the comment, so the remaining c */ is treated as code.
